questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly pairs each reciprocal trigonometric ratio with its definition in a right-angled triangle?

options.why: Confused cosecant with secant by incorrectly associating cosecant with cosine.
Listed the primary ratios sine, cosine, and tangent instead of their reciprocals.
Left secant as cosine (adjacent over hypotenuse) instead of inverting it.
Used the opposite side $20$ in place of the adjacent side, which gives $\operatorname{cosec}\theta=\frac{\text{hyp}}{\text{opp}}$.
Gave $\cos\theta=\frac{\text{adj}}{\text{hyp}}$ instead of inverting it to get $\sec\theta$.
Made both slips at once: used the opposite side and did not invert, giving $\sin\theta=\frac{\text{opp}}{\text{hyp}}$.

questions.question_text:
A right-angled triangle has a hypotenuse of length $10$ and an opposite side of length $6$ for an acute angle $\theta$.
What is the value of $\cot\theta$?

options.why: Calculated $\tan\theta=\frac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}}=\frac{6}{8}$ instead of $\cot\theta=\frac{\text{adj}}{\text{opp}}$.
Calculated $\sec\theta=\frac{\text{hyp}}{\text{adj}}=\frac{10}{8}$ instead of cotangent.
Calculated $\operatorname{cosec}\theta=\frac{\text{hyp}}{\text{opp}}=\frac{10}{6}$ instead of cotangent.

questions.question_text:
A right-angled triangle has opposite side $8$, adjacent side $15$ and hypotenuse $17$ relative to an acute angle $\theta$.
What is the value of $\sec\theta$?

options.why: Used the opposite side instead of the adjacent side, giving $\operatorname{cosec}\theta$.
Calculated $\cos\theta=\dfrac{\text{adj}}{\text{hyp}}$ instead of its reciprocal.
Calculated $\cot\theta=\dfrac{\text{adj}}{\text{opp}}$ instead of secant.

questions.question_text: For which of the following angles is $\operatorname{cosec}\theta$ undefined?

options.why: Used secant's rule that the ratio is undefined when cosine is zero, instead of cosecant's rule that sine must be zero.
Mistakenly treated equal opposite and adjacent sides, where $\tan45^{\circ}=1$, as making a reciprocal ratio undefined; division by zero is the condition.
Mistakenly treated the negative value $\sin270^{\circ}=-1$ as making its reciprocal undefined; only a zero denominator does that.

questions.solution_text:
$\operatorname{cosec}\theta=\dfrac{1}{\sin\theta}$ is undefined when $\sin\theta=0$.
$\sin 180^{\circ}=0$, so $\operatorname{cosec} 180^{\circ}$ is undefined.

questions.question_text:
In a right-angled triangle with acute angle $\phi$, the adjacent side is $12$ and the opposite side is $5$.
What is the value of $\operatorname{cosec}\phi$?

options.why: Used the adjacent side $12$ below the hypotenuse, which gives $\sec\phi=\frac{\text{hyp}}{\text{adj}}$ instead of cosecant.
Gave $\sin\phi=\frac{\text{opp}}{\text{hyp}}$ instead of inverting it to get the reciprocal ratio.
Made both slips at once: used the adjacent side and did not invert, giving $\cos\phi=\frac{\text{adj}}{\text{hyp}}$.

questions.question_text: What is the exact value of $\cot\left(-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)$?

options.why: Calculated $\tan(-2\pi/3)=\sqrt{3}$ instead of taking its reciprocal.
Dropped the negative sign of the supplied angle and evaluated $\cot(2\pi/3)$.
Dropped the negative sign of the angle and calculated $\tan(2\pi/3)$ instead of cotangent.
Confused cotangent with tangent; on the unit circle $\cot 270^{\circ}=\frac{x}{y}=\frac{0}{-1}=0$, whereas $\tan 270^{\circ}$ is undefined.
Assumed cotangent at quadrantal angles takes value $1$ rather than $\frac{x}{y}=\frac{0}{-1}=0$.
Used the value of $\sin 270^{\circ}=-1$ instead of computing $\frac{\cos 270^{\circ}}{\sin 270^{\circ}}=\frac{0}{-1}=0$.
The reciprocal of cosine is secant, not cosecant.
The reciprocal of tangent is cotangent, not cosecant.
This denotes inverse cosine, not the reciprocal of sine.
